tiers.name: Little
tiers.say: Little machine! Beep boop, picture puzzles!

tiers.name: Big
tiers.say: Big machine! Numbers and words, let's go!

tiers.name: Super
tiers.say: Super machine! Brain power, full blast!

rounds.say: Look at the loop! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Point and say it: red circle, blue square, red circle...
rounds.explain: Red circle, blue square, again and again!

rounds.say: Yellow star, purple star. Which star comes next?
rounds.hint: Say the colors out loud. Yellow, purple...
rounds.explain: Yellow, purple, yellow, purple. It loops!

rounds.say: Apple, fish, apple, fish. What comes next?
rounds.hint: What always comes after the apple?
rounds.explain: Apple, fish, apple, fish!

rounds.say: Look at the shapes on the belt. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Heart, circle, heart, circle. Keep saying it!
rounds.explain: Heart, circle, heart, circle. A shape loop!

rounds.say: Party loop! Which picture comes next?
rounds.hint: Balloon, cupcake... what comes after each cupcake?
rounds.explain: Balloon, cupcake, balloon. Party time!

rounds.say: How many ladybugs? Count them, then tap the number.
rounds.hint: Point to each ladybug as you count.
rounds.explain: One, two, three. Three ladybugs!

rounds.say: How many balloons? Tap the number you count.
rounds.hint: Count slowly. Point to each balloon just once.
rounds.explain: One, two, three, four balloons!

rounds.say: Count the flowers. How many are there?
rounds.hint: Point to each flower once as you count.
rounds.explain: Five flowers, like five fingers on one hand!

rounds.say: How many moons are in the sky? Tap the number.
rounds.hint: Point to each moon and count.
rounds.explain: One, two. Two moons!

rounds.say: Count up! What number comes next?
rounds.hint: Count out loud: one, two, three...
rounds.explain: One, two, three, four. Up by one!

rounds.say: Count up with the machine! What number comes next?
rounds.hint: Say the numbers out loud and keep going.
rounds.explain: Four, five, six, seven!

rounds.say: What number comes after nine?
rounds.hint: Count on your fingers: six, seven, eight, nine...
rounds.explain: Nine, then ten. Ten is all your fingers!

rounds.say: Which group has more apples?
rounds.hint: Count each group. The bigger number is more.
rounds.explain: Five apples is more than two!

rounds.say: Which group has fewer cupcakes? Fewer means not as many.
rounds.hint: Count each group. The smaller number is fewer.
rounds.explain: One is fewer than four!

rounds.say: Which group has more stars?
rounds.hint: Count the stars in each group.
rounds.explain: Six stars is more than three!

rounds.say: What comes next in the loop? Look closely!
rounds.hint: Count the fish before each ladybug.
rounds.explain: Fish, fish, ladybug. Two fish every time!

rounds.say: What comes next? Look at the colors.
rounds.hint: One red, then count the yellows.
rounds.explain: Red, yellow, yellow. One red, two yellow!

rounds.say: Three pictures take turns. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Find the other apples. What comes right after them?
rounds.explain: Apple, balloon, moon. A loop of three!

rounds.say: Which shape comes next in the loop?
rounds.hint: Say the shapes as you point. Circle, triangle...
rounds.explain: Circle, triangle, square, again and again!

rounds.say: What comes next? Watch the colors closely!
rounds.hint: Count the purple hearts before each green one.
rounds.explain: Purple, purple, green. Two purple every time!

rounds.say: How many fish? Only count the fish!
rounds.hint: Point to each fish as you count. Skip the apples.
rounds.explain: Four fish swimming by!

rounds.say: Count only the flowers. How many flowers are there?
rounds.hint: Point to each flower just once. Skip the apple.
rounds.explain: Seven flowers in the garden!

rounds.say: How many balloons? Only count the balloons!
rounds.hint: Point to each balloon. Skip the cupcakes.
rounds.explain: Five balloons for the party!

rounds.say: Night sky! How many yellow stars can you count?
rounds.hint: Point to each star. Skip the moons.
rounds.explain: Six twinkly stars!

rounds.say: A number fell off the belt! Which number is missing?
rounds.hint: Count from one. Which number did you skip?
rounds.explain: One, two, three, four, five!

rounds.say: Which number is missing from the belt?
rounds.hint: Count from six and listen for the gap.
rounds.explain: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten!

rounds.say: Count up with big numbers! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Say them out loud: eleven, twelve, thirteen...
rounds.explain: Thirteen, then fourteen. Up by one!

rounds.say: Which group has the most ladybugs?
rounds.hint: Count each group. Which number is the biggest?
rounds.explain: Four is the most!

rounds.say: Which group has the fewest flowers? Find the smallest group.
rounds.hint: Count each group. Which number is the smallest?
rounds.explain: Three is the fewest. It is less than four and five!

rounds.say: Which group has more? Count carefully!
rounds.hint: Count each group, then compare the numbers.
rounds.explain: Five balloons is more than four cupcakes!

rounds.say: Oh no, a gap in the loop! Which picture fills it?
rounds.hint: Find another cupcake. What comes right after it?
rounds.explain: Cupcake, ladybug, cloud. The loop is fixed!

rounds.say: Which shape fills the gap in the loop?
rounds.hint: One diamond, then count the hearts.
rounds.explain: Diamond, heart, heart. One, two, then again!

rounds.say: Which circle fixes the loop?
rounds.hint: Count the green circles. What comes after two greens?
rounds.explain: Green, green, yellow. The loop is fixed!

rounds.say: The first picture is missing! Which one goes at the start?
rounds.hint: Look at the loop. What always comes before the fish?
rounds.explain: Apple, fish, moon. The loop starts with apple!

rounds.say: Which picture is missing from the night sky loop?
rounds.hint: One moon, then count the clouds.
rounds.explain: Moon, cloud, cloud. One moon, two clouds!

rounds.say: How many fish? Only count the fish, nothing else!
rounds.hint: Point to each fish. Skip the apples and the ladybugs.
rounds.explain: Five fish! Great careful counting!

rounds.say: How many red hearts? Check the shape and the color!
rounds.hint: It must be red and a heart. Check each one.
rounds.explain: Four red hearts! The blue heart does not count.

rounds.say: Up in the sky! How many balloons can you find?
rounds.hint: Point to each balloon. Skip the clouds and the moon.
rounds.explain: Six balloons floating up high!

rounds.say: Garden time! How many ladybugs can you count?
rounds.hint: Point to each ladybug. Skip the flowers.
rounds.explain: Seven ladybugs in the garden!

rounds.say: Which number comes just before thirteen?
rounds.hint: Count back from thirteen. What comes just before?
rounds.explain: Twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen!

rounds.say: Count up! What number comes after nineteen?
rounds.hint: Start at sixteen. Say each number out loud.
rounds.explain: Nineteen, then twenty. Two tens!

rounds.say: Uh oh, a number is missing! Which one fits the gap?
rounds.hint: Count from fourteen and listen for the gap.
rounds.explain: Fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen!

rounds.say: Which group has more fish? Only count the fish!
rounds.hint: Count just the fish in each group. Skip the apples.
rounds.explain: Three fish is more than two fish!

rounds.say: Which group has the fewest clouds? Count carefully!
rounds.hint: Count each group. The smallest number is the fewest.
rounds.explain: Four is the fewest. It is less than five and six!

rounds.say: Which group has the most yellow stars?
rounds.hint: Count only the stars. Skip the moons.
rounds.explain: Four stars is the most!

rounds.say: Count by twos! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Add two to the last number.
rounds.explain: Two, four, six, eight, ten. Up by two!

rounds.say: Count by fives! What number comes next?
rounds.hint: Add five to the last number.
rounds.explain: Five, ten, fifteen, twenty. Up by five!

rounds.say: Count by tens! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Add ten to the last number.
rounds.explain: Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty!

rounds.say: Count back like a rocket! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Count down out loud: ten, nine, eight...
rounds.explain: Ten, nine, eight, seven, six. Counting down!

rounds.say: Which word rhymes with cake?
rounds.hint: Say each word out loud. Which one ends like cake?
rounds.explain: Cake and lake rhyme. They sound the same at the end!

rounds.say: Which word rhymes with star?
rounds.hint: Rhymes sound the same at the end. Say each one!
rounds.explain: Star and car rhyme!

rounds.say: What is the opposite of hot?
rounds.hint: Opposites are as different as can be.
rounds.explain: Hot and cold are opposites!

rounds.say: What is the opposite of up?
rounds.hint: Point up. Now point the other way!
rounds.explain: Up and down are opposites!

rounds.say: Put the two words together. What new word do they make?
rounds.hint: Read the first word, then the second, with no gap.
rounds.explain: Two small words make one big word: rainbow!

rounds.say: Glue the two words together. What word do they make?
rounds.hint: Say the two words fast, one after the other.
rounds.explain: Foot plus ball makes football!

rounds.say: Which letter is missing from the word robot?
rounds.hint: Say robot slowly: ro, bot.
rounds.explain: R, O, B, O, T spells robot!

rounds.say: What comes next in the loop?
rounds.hint: Look for pairs. Two of each!
rounds.explain: Two circles, two stars, again and again!

rounds.say: Four pictures take turns. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Find where the loop starts again.
rounds.explain: Apple, fish, balloon, moon. A loop of four!

rounds.say: Which group is all animals?
rounds.hint: Check every word. Is each one an animal?
rounds.explain: Dog, cow and owl are all animals!

rounds.say: Which group is all foods you can eat?
rounds.hint: Read carefully. One letter can change a word!
rounds.explain: Bread, pear and corn are all foods. Yum!

rounds.say: Put the words in order to make a sentence!
rounds.hint: The word with a capital letter goes first.
rounds.explain: Beep boop! A sentence starts with a capital letter.

rounds.say: Count by threes! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Add three to the last number.
rounds.explain: Three, six, nine, twelve. Up by three!

rounds.say: Count back by twos. Which number is missing?
rounds.hint: Each number is two less than the one before.
rounds.explain: Twenty, eighteen, sixteen, fourteen, twelve!

rounds.say: Which number is missing from the fives?
rounds.hint: Count by fives, starting at thirty-five.
rounds.explain: Forty, forty-five, fifty. Up by five!

rounds.say: Each number doubles! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Doubling means adding a number to itself.
rounds.explain: Eight plus eight is sixteen. Double!

rounds.say: Which word belongs in this word family?
rounds.hint: Look at how each word ends.
rounds.explain: Hop, mop, top and pop. Same ending, same family!

rounds.say: Which word joins this word family?
rounds.hint: Look at the last three letters of each word.
rounds.explain: Sing, ring, king, wing. The ing family!

rounds.say: One mouse, two what? Pick the right word.
rounds.hint: Some words change in a special way, like goose and geese.
rounds.explain: One mouse, two mice!

rounds.say: One box, two what? Pick the right spelling.
rounds.hint: Say it out loud. Do you hear an extra sound at the end?
rounds.explain: One box, two boxes. Words ending in x add e, s!

rounds.say: Which letter is missing from the word planet?
rounds.hint: Say it slowly: plan, et.
rounds.explain: P, L, A, N, E, T spells planet!

rounds.say: Which word finishes this compound word?
rounds.hint: Read the big word. What part comes before fly?
rounds.explain: Butter plus fly makes butterfly!

rounds.say: A puppy grows into a dog. What does a kitten grow into?
rounds.hint: Puppies and kittens are both baby animals.
rounds.explain: A kitten grows up to be a cat!

rounds.say: Which shape fixes the loop?
rounds.hint: Look for pairs. Every shape comes two at a time.
rounds.explain: Two triangles, two hearts. Pairs!

rounds.say: Which color is missing from the loop?
rounds.hint: Find the same spot in the first loop.
rounds.explain: Red, yellow, green, blue. A loop of four colors!

rounds.say: Which group is all things with wheels?
rounds.hint: Picture each one. Does it roll on wheels?
rounds.explain: Bikes, buses and wagons all have wheels!

rounds.say: Which group is all fruits?
rounds.hint: Fruits are sweet and grow on trees, bushes or vines.
rounds.explain: Pears, grapes and plums are all fruits!

rounds.say: Put the words in order to make a sentence!
rounds.hint: The capital letter goes first. The period goes last.
rounds.explain: What a sleepy cat! The period goes at the very end.

rounds.say: Make a sentence from the word cards!
rounds.hint: Who is playing? Start with that word.
rounds.explain: Splash! The sentence starts with who is playing.

rounds.say: The machine doubles each number. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Double means add the number to itself.
rounds.explain: Twenty-four plus twenty-four is forty-eight!

rounds.say: Count back by tens. Which number is missing?
rounds.hint: Each number is ten less than the one before.
rounds.explain: Eighty, seventy, sixty. Down by ten!

rounds.say: Find the jump size first. What comes next?
rounds.hint: How much bigger is each number than the one before?
rounds.explain: Up by four each time!

rounds.say: Count by twenty-fives! What comes next?
rounds.hint: Think of quarters. Add twenty-five each time.
rounds.explain: Four quarters make one hundred!

rounds.say: Count by sevens! What number comes next?
rounds.hint: Add seven to the last number.
rounds.explain: Seven, fourteen, twenty-one, twenty-eight!

rounds.say: Which word rhymes with bear? Say each word out loud!
rounds.hint: Say each word out loud. Rhymes can be spelled differently!
rounds.explain: Bear and chair rhyme, even with different spellings!

rounds.say: Which word rhymes with eight?
rounds.hint: Forget the spelling. Listen to the end sound.
rounds.explain: Eight and plate rhyme!

rounds.say: What is the opposite of float?
rounds.hint: Think about a heavy rock dropped in a pond.
rounds.explain: Float and sink are opposites!

rounds.say: One sheep, two what? This one is tricky!
rounds.hint: Some animal words stay exactly the same.
rounds.explain: One sheep, two sheep. It does not change!

rounds.say: One tooth, lots of what? Pick the right word.
rounds.hint: Some words change in the middle, like foot and feet.
rounds.explain: One tooth, many teeth. Brush them every day!

rounds.say: Eyes are for seeing. What are ears for?
rounds.hint: What do your ears do when a friend talks to you?
rounds.explain: We see with our eyes and hear with our ears!

rounds.say: Which letter is missing from the word dinosaur?
rounds.hint: Say it slowly: di, no, saur.
rounds.explain: D, I, N, O, S, A, U, R spells dinosaur. Roar!

rounds.say: This loop grows! Which picture fills the gap?
rounds.hint: Count the balloons after each cloud. One, two...
rounds.explain: One balloon, then two, then three. It grows!

rounds.say: Which shape is missing from the loop?
rounds.hint: Find the same spot in the second loop.
rounds.explain: Triangle, square, circle, diamond. A loop of four!

rounds.say: Which group is all things that can fly?
rounds.hint: Careful! Some birds cannot fly.
rounds.explain: Eagles, jets and bees all fly. Penguins swim instead!

rounds.say: Which group is all animals that live in the ocean?
rounds.hint: Picture where each animal lives.
rounds.explain: Whales, sharks and octopuses all live in the ocean!

rounds.say: Make a sentence about space!
rounds.hint: Start with the capital word. End with the period.
rounds.explain: Whoosh! Capital letter first, period last.

rounds.say: Put the words in order to ask a question!
rounds.hint: A question ends with a question mark.
rounds.explain: Questions end with a question mark!

rounds.say: Make a sentence about dinosaurs!
rounds.hint: Start with the capital word. When did they live?
rounds.explain: Roar! A long time ago tells when they lived.

rounds.say: Double trouble! Each number doubles. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Multiply the last number by two.
rounds.explain: Forty times two is eighty!

rounds.say: Now the machine cuts each number in half. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Half means split into two equal parts.
rounds.explain: Half of twelve is six!

rounds.say: Which number is missing from this pattern?
rounds.hint: Find the jump between the first two numbers.
rounds.explain: Up by fifteen each time, like minutes on a clock!

rounds.say: These are square numbers. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Multiply a number by itself: one times one, two times two...
rounds.explain: Five times five is twenty-five!

rounds.say: Count back by sevens. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Take seven away from the last number.
rounds.explain: Seventy-nine minus seven is seventy-two!

rounds.say: Which word means the same as fragile?
rounds.hint: Fragile things break easily, like a glass ornament.
rounds.explain: Fragile and delicate both mean easy to break!

rounds.say: Which word means the same as timid?
rounds.hint: A timid kitten hides when visitors come over.
rounds.explain: Timid and shy both mean easily scared!

rounds.say: Which word is the opposite of generous?
rounds.hint: Generous people love to share. Who does not?
rounds.explain: Generous people share. Selfish people do not!

rounds.say: Which word is the opposite of ancient?
rounds.hint: Ancient means very, very old. Look for the word that means new.
rounds.explain: Ancient means very old. Modern means new and up to date!

rounds.say: Bird goes with nest. Bee goes with what?
rounds.hint: Think about where each animal lives.
rounds.explain: Birds live in nests. Bees live in hives!

rounds.say: Pick the right spelling to finish the sentence.
rounds.hint: This word shows that something belongs to them.
rounds.explain: Their means it belongs to them!

rounds.say: Shapes and colors loop at different speeds. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Check the shape loop first, then the color loop.
rounds.explain: Shapes repeat every two. Colors repeat every three!

rounds.say: Which group is all verbs, or action words?
rounds.hint: Try putting I can in front of each word.
rounds.explain: Whisper, climb and explore are all actions!

rounds.say: Which group is all adjectives, or describing words?
rounds.hint: Put each word before the word dog. Does it describe it?
rounds.explain: Brave, shiny and gentle all describe things!

rounds.say: Put the words in order. Watch the comma!
rounds.hint: The comma ends the first part of the sentence.
rounds.explain: Sparkly! The comma comes right after the when part.

rounds.say: Make an excited sentence. Watch the comma!
rounds.hint: Start with the word that shows surprise.
rounds.explain: Exclamation marks show excitement!

rounds.say: These are cube numbers. Which one is missing?
rounds.hint: Multiply a number by itself, then by itself again.
rounds.explain: Four times four times four is sixty-four!

rounds.say: Each jump is one bigger than the last. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Look at the jumps: two, then three, then four.
rounds.explain: Add five this time. Ten plus five is fifteen!

rounds.say: Each number comes from the two before it. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Add the last two numbers together.
rounds.explain: Five plus eight is thirteen!

rounds.say: Two rules take turns in this machine. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Look at the jumps. Up three, then down one.
rounds.explain: Up three, down one, again and again!

rounds.say: What rule is the machine using? What comes next?
rounds.hint: Compare each number with the one before. How many times bigger?
rounds.explain: Times three each time. Eighteen times three is fifty-four!

rounds.say: Which beginning makes a word that means heat before?
rounds.hint: Think of an oven warming up before baking cookies.
rounds.explain: Preheat means to heat before. Pre means before!

rounds.say: Which beginning makes a word that means not agree?
rounds.hint: Add each beginning to agree. Which makes a real word?
rounds.explain: Disagree means not agree!

rounds.say: Which ending makes a word that means without care?
rounds.hint: One ending means full of. Another means without.
rounds.explain: Careless means without care!

rounds.say: Which ending makes a word for a person who teaches?
rounds.hint: Think of a baker, a singer and a painter.
rounds.explain: A teacher is a person who teaches!

rounds.say: Pick the right spelling to finish the sentence.
rounds.hint: This spelling means very, or also.
rounds.explain: Too means very. The soup is too hot to eat!

rounds.say: Glove goes with hand. Helmet goes with what?
rounds.hint: Think about which body part each one protects.
rounds.explain: Gloves cover hands. Helmets protect heads!

rounds.say: Two loops are mixed together. Which picture fills the gap?
rounds.hint: Shapes repeat every three. Colors repeat every two.
rounds.explain: Triangle, heart, star for shapes. Orange, purple for colors!

rounds.say: Find the shape loop and the color loop. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Say just the shapes. Then say just the colors.
rounds.explain: Square, circle, triangle and blue, yellow. Two loops!

rounds.say: Which group is all nouns, or naming words?
rounds.hint: A noun can follow the word the. Try each word.
rounds.explain: Courage is a noun too, even though you cannot touch it!

rounds.say: Which group is all mammals?
rounds.hint: Mammals breathe air and feed their babies milk.
rounds.explain: Whales and bats are mammals, just like horses!

rounds.say: Put the words in order. Start with when it happened!
rounds.hint: The comma comes right after the day of the week.
rounds.explain: Roar! The when part comes first, then a comma.

rounds.say: Prime numbers divide evenly only by one and themselves. Which prime comes next?
rounds.hint: Start at twelve and count up. Stop at the very first prime.
rounds.explain: Thirteen is the next prime number!

rounds.say: Two different rules take turns here. What comes next?
rounds.hint: Compare each pair of numbers. One step multiplies, one step adds.
rounds.explain: Times two, then plus one. Fourteen plus one is fifteen!

rounds.say: Crack the code! What number comes next?
rounds.hint: Look at three numbers in a row. How are they linked?
rounds.explain: Add the two before. Eleven plus eighteen is twenty-nine!

rounds.say: The machine counts back by threes. What comes after zero?
rounds.hint: Numbers keep going below zero, like on a cold thermometer.
rounds.explain: Below zero comes negative three!

rounds.say: Which square number is missing?
rounds.hint: Which number times itself makes each one?
rounds.explain: Seven times seven is forty-nine!

rounds.say: Which word means the same as weary?
rounds.hint: Weary is how you feel after a very long hike.
rounds.explain: Weary means very tired!

rounds.say: Which word is the opposite of accept?
rounds.hint: Watch out for a word that only looks similar!
rounds.explain: Accept means say yes. Refuse means say no!

rounds.say: Pick the right spelling to start the sentence.
rounds.hint: Try saying they are in the gap. Does it fit?
rounds.explain: They're is short for they are!

rounds.say: Pick the right spelling for the sentence.
rounds.hint: You win by a number of points. Which spelling is the number after seven?
rounds.explain: Eight is the number. Ate is eating. Eighth is a place in line!

rounds.say: Author goes with book. Composer goes with what?
rounds.hint: An author writes books. What does a composer write?
rounds.explain: Authors write books. Composers write songs!

rounds.say: Which ending turns kind into a naming word, a noun?
rounds.hint: Try each one in: She showed great blank.
rounds.explain: Kindness is a noun. You can show kindness!

rounds.say: Which beginning makes a word that means behave badly?
rounds.hint: Add each beginning to behave. Which makes a real word?
rounds.explain: Misbehave means behave badly. Mis means wrongly!

rounds.say: Two loops are tangled together. Which picture fills the gap?
rounds.hint: Find the shape loop. Then find the color loop.
rounds.explain: Heart, star for shapes. Blue, orange, green for colors!

rounds.say: Which group is all adverbs, words that tell how?
rounds.hint: Careful! Some words end in L Y but still describe things.
rounds.explain: Slowly, quietly and bravely tell how. Lovely and friendly describe things!

rounds.say: Which group is all words that mean happy?
rounds.hint: Read every word. The other groups each hide a word that is not happy.
rounds.explain: Joyful, cheerful and glad all mean happy!

rounds.say: Build a tricky sentence. Use the comma as a clue!
rounds.hint: Start with Although. The comma ends the first part.
rounds.explain: Brrr! The comma ends the first part.

rounds.say: Make a long sentence about the beach!
rounds.hint: Start with where it happened. Then say who did it.
rounds.explain: Great building! The where part comes first, then a comma.
